hook: Bones are rewriting two decades of human history through ancient DNA.

sections.voiceover: Bones are rewriting two decades of human history through ancient DNA.
b_roll: ancient bone specimens in a laboratory archive

sections.voiceover: In 1950, radiocarbon dating transformed archaeology forever. Yichen Liu and Xiaowei Mao watched laboratories expand that archive. Who migrated and who conquered, Qiaomei Fu?
b_roll: DNA sequencing lab with researchers Yichen Liu and Xiaowei Mao

sections.voiceover: Yet Razib Khan reported in Quillette how genetics settled long arguments.
Curry calls paleogenomics the biggest development in archaeology since radiocarbon dating. Johannes Krause documented this rapid temporal expansion in Science.
b_roll: National Geographic magazine featuring Andrew Curry
Science journal article by Johannes Krause and Qiaomei Fu

sections.voiceover: Read Science to see ancient DNA archives rewrite human history.
